heard: Nearly 200 men at the Alamo faced a blood-red flag. In 1836, William Travis answered surrender demands with cannon fire. Travis pleaded for help, 32 men from Gonzales arrived but he still needed more. At dawn, about 1,800 attackers breached the crumbling walls. Within 90 minutes, the final assault was over. On April 21, Texian troops won at San Jacinto in under 20 minutes. They remembered the men who faced that blood-red flag.
